solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Principally masculine sort like this with power? No

definitions.text: Principally masculine sort like this with power? No

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, at the start, so only the opening letter of masculine is taken

parts.note: sort means kind, as does ilk
like this means so, as in 'do it so'
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A question about whether a manly type with power fits a description, answered with a flat no.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a male who is not at all masculine and has no power, as the closing 'No' insists.
explanation.definitionFit: A milquetoast weakling is the very opposite of a powerful masculine type, which the clue's final denial points to.

clue.text: Passion, oddly ardent, getting into hot water …

indicators.note: getting into means those letters go inside the trouble word

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in a mess

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of ardent

explanation.surface: An ardent passion that lands someone in hot water.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion in its old sense of frenzy or rage is a kind of insanity.

clue.text: … arising from affaire, it's ultimately more passionate

indicators.note: arising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, an affair turns out to be the hotter one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'arising' means reading upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative of a word meaning lustful or vigorous, so more full of desire.

clue.text: Total of love-god mounting when touring clubs

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the reversed god surrounds the clubs letter
mounting in a down clue means going up, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Cupid's tally of conquests climbing as he tours the nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tally of points in a game is a sum, the same as a total.

clue.text: French courtesy seeing drunk English in gang

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the gang word

parts.note: a posse is a gang
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: French politeness on show when a drunk Englishman joins a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means formal good manners or politeness.

clue.text: Feline ace to finish hard harnessing explosive energy

definitions.text: Feline ace to finish hard harnessing explosive energy

indicators.note: harnessing means holding in, so the explosive and energy letters go inside
to finish says the ace is shifted to the end of the feline word

parts.note: a feline is a cat
an ace is the A card
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
E is the physics symbol for energy
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A champion big cat that finishes strongly with bursts of explosive energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish' sends the ace to the end of the feline word, and 'harnessing' sets the explosive and energy letters inside; the whole clue also describes the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This spotted African cat is famed for its explosive sprinting speed, so the whole clue paints it.

clue.text: Break up about love without love

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: without means the second love is removed from the first

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Splitting up over a relationship that has lost its love.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'love' is the word itself and the second is O, a tennis nil.
explanation.definitionFit: When a glacier or ice shelf sheds a chunk, it is said to break up in this way.

clue.text: Free spare time holding nearly glacial sweetheart

indicators.note: holding means the spare and time letters contain the glacial letters

parts.note: spare means extra

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: glacial means icy
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: Using spare time to win over a frosty sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' has spare-plus-time wrap the trimmed glacial word; 'sweetheart' gives only the central letter of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: To release someone from a tangle or difficulty is to free them.

clue.text: Study period in India ends

parts.note: a school or university term is a period of study
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A student's term in India comes to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: The end points of a line or route are its terminals, a plural noun matching ends.

clue.text: Wretched worker takes good advance being promoted

indicators.note: takes means takes in, so the worker word holds the good letter

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker

indicators.note: promoted means raised, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: to advance is to go

explanation.surface: A miserable employee gets a nice advance on promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced and miserable, as of someone wretched.

clue.text: Pillage of French land besieging leader from Paris

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the land word wraps the Paris letter

parts.note: land means earth or soil

indicators.note: the leader from a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A French army besieging the capital and looting the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillage is to plunder or strip a place of its valuables, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Palace in Italy stripped back, Pope finally managed

indicators.note: back says the stripped letters are read in reverse
stripped means the outer letters of Italy are removed, leaving the inside
finally picks the last letter of Pope

parts.note: managed as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A papal palace in Italy, stripped bare, with the Pope finally coping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palace in Italy' looks like one definition, but Italy is the fodder, stripped of its outer letters and read 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran Palace in Rome was the principal papal residence for centuries.

clue.text: Grand opening not ending trembling heart

parts.note: grand means epic, on a heroic scale

indicators.note: not ending means the last letter of the opening word is dropped

parts.note: an entrée is an opening or way in

explanation.surface: A grand opening night that leaves the heart trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembling' is not an anagram signal here: it is part of the definition, the point where an earthquake shakes hardest.
explanation.definitionFit: The point on the surface above an earthquake's focus is where the shaking is centred.

clue.text: Long story after single call flipping ends

parts.note: single means one, the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: flipping ends says the first and last letters of the call word swap places

parts.note: to call someone on the phone is to dial

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale told after a lone phone call that ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping ends' swaps only the first and last letters of the call word; 'after' just places it behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem about the Trojan War is a famously long narrative.

clue.text: Force men on ship, half cut

indicators.note: in an across clue A on B puts A after B
half cut means half of the ship abbreviation is removed

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
the men on a ship are its crew

explanation.surface: Sailors forced aboard a ship, half drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' is British slang for tipsy, but here it halves SS to S; the men then follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw money out of someone is to extort it, to force them to pay.

clue.text: Why the woman's iron's returned, corroded outside

indicators.note: outside means the corroded word goes around the rest

parts.note: corroded means wore away
her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: returned means the iron symbol is turned back

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Asking why a woman's iron came back rusted on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes mislead: 'the woman's' is the possessive pronoun, and 'iron's returned' means the iron symbol is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for for what reason, as in Juliet's famous question.

clue.text: Marine's brutal, taking area with force

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the brutal word holds the other letters

parts.note: searing criticism is harsh or brutal
F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A Royal Marine is brutal, seizing territory by force.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things to do with the sea and ships, as in a nautical or ocean-going people.

clue.text: With a facility consuming globules, small to start

definitions.text: With a facility consuming globules, small to start

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the facility word holds the globule letters

parts.note: a bent is a natural facility or aptitude

indicators.note: to start says the small letter goes to the front

parts.note: globules are small spheres or orbs

explanation.surface: Something with a knack for soaking up little drops, starting small.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a sponge-like material; 'to start' moves S to the front of ORBS, giving SORB.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to soak up liquid droplets readily has exactly the capacity the clue describes.

clue.text: Untiring church without support when bishop leaves

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: bishop leaves means the B is taken out

parts.note: baseless means having no foundation or support
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An untiring church carrying on without funding once its bishop departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untiring never stops, the same as being unending or incessant.

clue.text: Particular potato topping for each, full of beans

indicators.note: topping means placed above, so in a down clue it comes first

parts.note: a chip is a single piece of fried potato
per means for each

explanation.surface: A particular potato dish topped for each serving, packed with beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of beans' is British for lively, not a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheerful and lively is an informal British meaning of being full of energy.

clue.text: Sailor back out East quit

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: out means the east letter is removed

parts.note: to back someone is to second them
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A sailor backing out of the East and leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away secretly, leaving a place for good, is to quit it.

clue.text: Follow logic without principal around university

indicators.note: around means the trimmed word goes round the university letter
without principal means losing the leading letter

parts.note: logic is good sense

explanation.surface: Following an argument without its key premise around a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' is the first letter, not a head of college: SENSE loses S to give ENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after as a consequence is to result or succeed, as in what follows.

clue.text: Queen raised under house housing cold staff

indicators.note: under places the queen letters below, after them in a down clue
housing means containing, so the house holds the cold letter

parts.note: a sept is a clan or house

indicators.note: raised means read upwards, reversing the letters

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A queen raised beneath a house that keeps cold staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental rod carried by a monarch is a ceremonial staff.

clue.text: Hardline former Tories meet occasionally

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of the following words

explanation.surface: Hardliners from the old Conservatives get together now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardline position is uncompromising, at the far end of opinion.

clue.text: Independent's petition for publication

parts.note: I for independent plus S from the apostrophe s
to sue is to petition a court

explanation.surface: A newspaper petition submitted for print.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition of a magazine or newspaper is a single number put out for readers.

clue.text: Stout heart receives tug, almost not heartless

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so the tug letters go inside

parts.note: the heart of something is its core

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tug is a pull

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of not is removed

explanation.surface: A brave heart takes on a tug of war that almost proves heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout here means fat or portly, describing a heavily built body.

clue.text: Beaten by scoundrel without once dropping odds

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the scoundrel goes round

parts.note: a cad is a scoundrel

indicators.note: dropping odds keeps only the even-numbered letters of once

explanation.surface: Beaten by a villain without ever once losing a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, an old sense, not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck with a stick as punishment is being beaten.

clue.text: Usually least tolerant radical activist initially

definitions.text: Usually least tolerant radical activist initially

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A radical activist is usually the least tolerant one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radical activist' is the definition but also supplies R and A, so the whole clue does both jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holding views at the far edge of a movement is typically intolerant.

clue.text: One could be one

parts.note: the word one, used as in 'one should', is itself a part of speech standing in for a noun

explanation.surface: A riddling remark that anybody might be anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'one' is the word itself: in 'one never knows' it stands in for a person, which makes it this part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A word replacing a noun, such as he, it or one, belongs to this grammatical class.

clue.text: Term of endearment? It legitimises embracing

indicators.note: embracing means the following words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A pet name that makes a relationship official by its very embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term of endearment' looks like the definition, but 'Term' alone is, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To term something is to name or call it, the same as giving it a title.

clue.text: Ginger beer half knocked back's flat, admits husband

indicators.note: knocked back means those letters are turned around
half here takes the second half of beer
admits means lets in, so the husband letter goes inside

parts.note: a flat battery is dead

explanation.surface: A ginger beer half drunk and now flat, with a husband let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger beer' reads as a drink, but 'Ginger' alone is a person with red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is an informal British name for someone with orange-red hair.

clue.text: Swing door needing oil, we hear

parts.note: a trapdoor is a trap

indicators.note: we hear says the following word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to oil a mechanism is to ease it

explanation.surface: A squeaky swing door that needs oiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swing door' reads as one thing; 'Swing' is the definition, a circus bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar slung from two ropes is the swing used by circus acrobats.
